title: The Morning Digest: November 11, 2026
dek: Brent Jan27 settled at $91.49 on Tuesday, down $1.08 or 1.2 percent, and WTI Dec26 settled at $86.04, down $0.81 or 0.9 percent, both the lowest closes since Aug 31 (Reuters, Nov 11; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 10), and Wednesday's Asian session firmed to $92.01 and $86.20 on the latest Reuters snapshot (0730 GMT). Tuesday's intraday low took Brent below $90 before a partial recovery. January WCS is -$24.40 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 10), wider by $1.05 on 895 lots, the first traded widening after four tightening sessions, while December marked tighter to -$28.49 on zero lots. The API bulletin printed a 9.0 million barrel crude build and a 1.5 million barrel distillate build for the week ending Nov 6. The validated diesel crack is $89.08.

sources.vintage: Nov 11, 2026 (Tuesday settles: Brent Jan27 $91.49, down $1.08 or 1.2 percent; WTI Dec26 $86.04, down $0.81 or 0.9 percent; both the lowest closes since Aug 31; Brent to WTI spread $5.45 at the settle; Wednesday snapshots: Brent $92.53 and WTI $86.71 at 0420 GMT, Brent $92.01 and WTI $86.20 at 0730 GMT)

Nov 10, 2026 (Tuesday intraday: Brent fell more than $3 and briefly below $90, down as much as 3.7 percent, before recovering part of the loss after an Iranian security official said no talks were taking place; premiums for physical barrels are falling and tanker costs declining; US gasoline below $4 a gallon for the first time since July; Kpler positioning: trend-following CTA length in Brent cut to 9 percent long on Tuesday from 45 percent at Monday's end, WTI also cut to 9 percent)
